title: Microsoft Entra ID: passkey sign-in to Microsoft apps on Android through Authenticator or Company Portal
summary: Hold: the briefing incorrectly assures readers that older Android devices fall back to other sign-in methods. Conditional Access can instead block access when a user cannot use a method that satisfies the required authentication strength. The broker compatibility, licensing, roadmap facts and listed control operations are supported, but two additional descriptions need narrowing.

claims.claim: Microsoft Entra ID users can use passkeys in Microsoft apps on Android with a broker such as Microsoft Authenticator or Microsoft Intune Company Portal installed.
claims.quote: Microsoft Entra ID users can now use a passkey to sign into Microsoft apps on Android devices where an authentication broker like Microsoft Authenticator or Microsoft Intune Company Portal is installed.

claims.claim: The Entra admin center route through Security, Authentication methods, Policies, Passkey (FIDO2), Enable and Target and Add target reaches target passkey-profile assignment.
claims.quote:
Browse to Entra ID > Security > Authentication methods > Policies.
Select Passkey (FIDO2).
Select Enable and Target.
Select Add target, and then choose All users or Select targets to choose specific groups.
Select the passkey profiles that you want to assign to a specific target.

claims.claim: Entra ID > Authentication methods > Authentication strengths > New authentication strength > Passkeys (FIDO2) is the documented custom-strength route.
claims.quote:
Browse to Entra ID > Authentication methods > Authentication strengths.
Select New authentication strength.
Provide a Name for your new authentication strength.
Optionally provide a Description.
Select Passkeys (FIDO2).

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/policies/authenticationStrengthPolicies creates a custom strength specifying permitted authentication methods.
claims.quote:
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/policies/authenticationStrengthPolicies
"allowedCombinations": [
        "fido2"
    ]
claims.fix: Keep the call unchanged. Append to controls[2].note and the rendered row note: 'The request body sets allowedCombinations to ["fido2"] to permit passkeys (FIDO2).'

claims.where: controls[2].note; Why it matters; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: A custom strength is enforced for protected resources by using it in a Conditional Access policy, rather than merely creating it.
claims.quote: After defining the authentication strength policy, you apply and enforce it for the protected resource using Microsoft Entra conditional access policies.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/resources/authenticationstrengths-overview?view=graph-rest-1.0 to sources for the distinction between defining a strength and applying it through Conditional Access.

claims.claim: After opting in to passkey profiles, an administrator cannot opt out.
claims.quote: After you opt in to enable passkey profiles, you can't opt out.

claims.claim: Membership in an excluded group blocks passkey registration and sign-in entirely.
claims.quote: If a user is a member of an excluded group in the Passkeys (FIDO2) authentication method policy, they're blocked from FIDO2 passkey registration or sign-in entirely

claims.claim: Excluded-group membership takes precedence over included-group membership in the Passkey (FIDO2) policy.
claims.quote: this takes precedence over them being in any Included groups.

claims.where: Governance controls; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Removing a previously allowed AAGUID prevents users from signing in with the previously registered method.
claims.quote: If you change key restrictions and remove an AAGUID that you previously allowed, users who previously registered an allowed method can no longer use it for sign-in.

claims.claim: Group-based passkey profiles configure passkey types, attestation and provider restrictions by AAGUID.
claims.quote: Passkey profiles enable granular group-based configurations for passkey (FIDO2) authentication. Instead of a single tenant-wide setting, you can define specific requirements such as attestation, passkey type (device-bound or synced), or Authenticator Attestation GUID (AAGUID) restrictions.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Passkeys provide phishing-resistant authentication.
claims.quote: Passkeys are FIDO2-based credentials that provide strong, phishing-resistant authentication.

claims.claim: Passkeys in Microsoft Authenticator are device-bound.
claims.quote: Passkeys in the Authenticator app are device-bound to ensure that they never leave the device they were created on.

claims.claim: Authenticator creates Android passkeys in the Secure Element when supported, otherwise in the Trusted Execution Environment.
claims.quote: On Android, we create the passkey in the Secure Element on devices that support it, or fall back to the Trusted Execution Environment (TEE).

claims.claim: Older devices fall back to other authentication methods.
claims.quote: If the authentication strength doesn't include a method that the user can register and use, Microsoft Entra ID blocks the user from signing in to the resource.
claims.fix: Remove 'Older devices fall back to other methods.' Alternatively replace it with 'Another sign-in method must satisfy the applicable authentication strength; if no included method can be registered and used, Microsoft Entra ID blocks access.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/authentication/concept-authentication-strength-how-it-works for that replacement.

claims.claim: Passkey registration is not supported for internal or external guest users.
claims.quote: Registration of passkey (FIDO2) credentials isn't supported for internal or external guest users, including B2B collaboration users in the resource tenant.

claims.claim: The previous passkey gap pushed Android users of Outlook, Teams and OneDrive back to weaker methods.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Android Outlook Teams OneDrive passkeys previously weaker methods broker support'; read the matrix, Authenticator sign-in guide and October 2024 Entra release-archive excerpt. They establish passkey support, not this historical fallback to weaker methods.
claims.fix: Replace the first sentence of Why it matters with 'A supported broker enables passkey sign-in in Outlook, Teams and OneDrive on Android.'

claims.claim: Users see the passkey sign-in option only if the Passkey (FIDO2) policy allows them a passkey.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Microsoft Entra passkey sign in option visible users not enabled authentication methods policy'; read passkey enablement and Authenticator sign-in. These establish permission to register or authenticate, not that the sign-in option is hidden from every ineligible user.
claims.fix: Replace 'Users see the option only if the Passkey (FIDO2) policy allows them a passkey, and each user chooses whether to use it' with 'Users must be allowed by the Passkey (FIDO2) policy to register and sign in with a passkey; eligible users can choose passkey sign-in.'
